diagnosis: Accelerate scheduler semantics advanced the wrapped scheduler once per process per synchronized optimizer update. A global 200-step cosine horizon was passed unscaled under two-process DDP, so the schedule reached its endpoint at approximately global step 100 and then continued into the next cosine half-cycle.
builder_lesson: A zero exit code is not proof of a scientifically valid learning run. Inspect learning-control telemetry such as LR, loss, token counts, and checkpoint lineage. Preserve useful learned weights, repair the smallest actual control defect, and resume rather than restart.
repair: express schedule horizons in global optimizer updates
translate to Accelerate-internal scheduler steps using process count when split_batches is false
separate checkpoint segment end from LR horizon
compare deterministic held-out evaluation before and after the next segment
teaching_policy: Expand teacher data against observed capability gaps, not row-count targets. First close registry coverage gaps, then use per-competency failures to decide future Sol examples.
